title: Sonny and the Long Grass Sea | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the quokka finds a wide moonlit meadow where the long grass ripples like a silver sea in the wind, and she lies down in it and lets the gentle sound carry her to sleep. A dreamy tale from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales for little ones ready to drift off.
narration:
The moon had risen, round and full and bright, over the edge of the bush. Little Sonny the quokka had been following a path through the trees, and now she stepped out into somewhere she had never been before — the very edge of a wide, wide meadow.

The grass was long and pale, almost silver in the moonlight. And when the wind moved through it, the whole meadow moved too — a soft, slow wave that rolled from one side all the way across to the other, just like the sea.

Sunny stood very still at the edge and watched.

The grass rippled. Then settled. Then rippled again from a new direction, another wave following the first, just like the sea does when it is very calm and the wind is very gentle.

The sound it made was soft. A quiet, dry whisper — shhh — as each wave passed through. And then again. Shhh. Over and over, slow and steady, like something breathing. Like the whole meadow was breathing.

Sunny took one careful step into the grass. Then another. The long blades bent softly around her, and the sound of the whispering filled her ears from every side at once.

She lay down.

The grass swayed slowly all around her. The shushing continued, soft and even. And the whole meadow seemed to rock, very gently, like a small boat on still water. Rocking just a little. Just enough.

The moon was bright above. The stars were bright. The grass was moving, and the world was soft, and Sunny closed her eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, long grass sea. Goodnight, little one.
